service.name: Wedding cocktail hour music in Denver
service.serviceType: Live music for wedding cocktail hours in Denver
service.description: Jazz duo and solo guitarist bookings for wedding cocktail hours at Denver hotels, galleries, gardens, mansions and event floors, with no metro travel line.

faqs.q: Where do Denver wedding cocktail hours usually happen?
faqs.a: In the pause between ceremony and reception: hotel lobbies and mezzanines downtown, gallery floors in the Santa Fe arts district, garden terraces at the Botanic Gardens, and the parlors of Capitol Hill mansions. A duo fits all of them; the footprint is eight feet by six.

faqs.q: What does load-in look like at a downtown Denver venue?
faqs.a: It's small and early. A duo loads in within 60 minutes through the service entrance, plays on an 8 by 6 foot footprint, and runs on one dedicated 20-amp circuit. We settle dock windows and freight elevators with the venue before the day, so no cases cross the lobby.

faqs.q: Is there a travel charge for a Denver wedding?
faqs.a: No. Denver is our home market, so a metro date carries no travel line. Travel appears on a quote only outside the metro: Boulder and Colorado Springs are a short Front Range line, and mountain venues carry their own line.

faqs.q: Can the duo play an outdoor cocktail hour at a Denver garden venue?
faqs.a: Yes, on a covered, level and dry performance area with power run to it. Denver evenings get cold fast after sunset, so the weather call and the move-indoors time are written before the day. Garden terraces with a pavilion make this the easiest outdoor booking on the calendar.

faqs.q: Is a duo enough for a cocktail hour at a Denver hotel?
faqs.a: Yes, for the guest counts these buildings hold at cocktail hour. Two musicians hold 65 to 72 dBA across a lobby lounge or a mezzanine, and the hour rarely gets the main floor anyway because the main floor is being set for dinner. The trio is the size to book when the crowd spreads across a full ballroom.

faqs.q: Can guests talk over live music on a Denver garden terrace?
faqs.a: Yes, and outdoors makes it easier. Open air has no walls to hand the sound back, so the level guests hear is the level the musicians set, and that's a volume two people who have just met can talk across. What outdoors does need is a covered, level and dry performance area with power run to it.
